scope_plain: Only voters who live inside Tallahassee city limits; the whole city votes on each seat. If you live outside city limits (even with a Tallahassee mailing address), these races aren't on your ballot.
office_explainer: Chairs the five-member City Commission and votes with it on city laws, the budget and city services.
why_it_matters: Open seat: Mayor John Dailey did not run. WFSU calls the runoff "an ideological battle": Matlow is part of the commission's progressive minority bloc, and Ausley is "a Democratic moderate."

candidates.name: Loranne Ausley
candidates.background: Former state senator (2020 to 2022) and state representative; 14 years in the Legislature. Attorney and founder of Whole Child Leon. Finished second on Aug 18 with 33.7% (13,988 votes).

own_words.text: "We continue with our message of civility and working together to find common ground to move this community forward."
"People want progress without division. They want opportunity without losing what makes this place special."
Says Tallahassee should expand private-sector jobs so young people have reasons to stay after graduating.

candidates.name: Jeremy Matlow
candidates.background: City commissioner (Seat 3) since 2018 and owner of local restaurants, including Gaines Street Pies. Finished first on Aug 18 with 36.0% (14,934 votes).

own_words.text: "We're ready for a government that looks after everyday people, doesn't bend over for the same special interests."
"Add affordable housing by building 500 municipal units available to all income brackets."
"We have to make our community something that young people want to be a part of."

scope_plain: Only voters who live inside Tallahassee city limits; the whole city votes on each seat. If you live outside city limits (even with a Tallahassee mailing address), these races aren't on your ballot.
office_explainer: One of five citywide commissioners who pass city laws and the budget and hire the city manager.
why_it_matters: Open seat: Matlow is leaving it to run for mayor. Perez was part of Matlow's "progressive coalition" on primary night (WFSU); Derzypolski says he wants to end "teams and factions and 3-2 votes." With the mayor's seat and Seat 5 also on the ballot, the result helps decide the commission's often-discussed 3-2 split (WFSU).

candidates.name: Tom Derzypolski
candidates.background: Co-founder and owner of BowStern, a Tallahassee communications firm; eight years as a U.S. Navy corpsman; former local Red Cross chair. Finished second on Aug 18 with 10,533 votes, 15 ahead of Talethia Edwards after a manual recount.

own_words.text: "It's time for a new way of governing where we do so leading with respect."
"You can't stay here if there's not a career here for you."
"Lower bills. Fewer unnecessary fees. More money left over at the end of the month."

candidates.name: P.J. Perez
candidates.background: Public school teacher for about 15 years, now at Tallahassee Collegiate Academy; after graduating from FSU he worked with neighborhoods on Tallahassee's south side. Finished first on Aug 18 with 11,634 votes (29.1%).

own_words.text: On the commission's 3-2 split: "most people just want to know... how we're going to tackle affordability."
"You can't have just copy-paste national chains all around."
"I support a moratorium on large AI data centers."
